recent_decisions.decision: THE FAR RUNG DESIGN (perf arc increment 4, the orbit speckles) went through a 5-agent panel (3 diagnoses + contract + adversarial critique, 1.27M tokens, 86 min) and the critique returned NEEDS_REVISION with 8 blockers, so the implementers were NOT launched on the v1 contract. Diagnosis of record: the speckles are the constructed bodies (cloud_v2_body) point-sampled at footprints 2 to 20x their size (CLOUD_V2_FADE_LO/HI 3.9/4.0 keeps them at full weight under 15 km footprints); the noise body is already band-limited by its mip chain, the built body has no prefiltered representation. The far rung = a planet-fixed PROFILE (per lattice cell and height bin: cloud fraction f and mean density G of the same field the march renders) in an RGBA8 atlas of six nested windows + one global equirect map with mips, read by lodb, integrated in transmittance by a clumped-medium element law (fraction + in-cloud density; a plain mean fed to Beer-Lambert is the white-veil class), skipping density AND the sun ladder at w=1. Blockers found by the critique and the orchestrator's v2 decisions (scratchpad farrung-amendments.md, folded into docs/design/cloud-far-rung.md by a revision agent): (B1) the bake cost was understated ~100x (uncached SDF point tests per texel: a level-5 bake ~2.8 s, the global ~85 s) -> A1 analytic per-cloud ellipses from a runtime CALIBRATION table (canonical archetype cross-section radius + mean density baked once from the shipped SDF), cell-stratified ellipse tests at fine levels; (B2) the element law was not step-invariant (ln T ~ seg^2) -> A7 tau_elem = sigma D L_elem, T = pow(1 - w f (1 - e^-tau_elem), seg/L_elem), with a prove-red on eco 0 vs 1; (B3) the shell draw's group 3 binding 0 is the temporal accumulation map, so the profile's group cannot carry the sun atlas there -> A8 a b14 override on the albedo-group builder, every group variant rebuilt; (B4) map_diag 1 writes OPAQUE greyscale, alpha is always 1, so three gates would have passed vacuously -> A9 luminance thresholds, calibrated red on v0.1288 first; (B5) the G5 speckle target (50) was below the metric's no-cloud floor (263) -> A10 at or below High's own count (252) and mass (0.152%) on the map_diag 1 render, and the census promoted to scripts/cloud-speckle-census.js (reproduces every baseline: eco0 2464, eco1 2989, High 252, off 263); (B6) albedo_sampler mip filter is Nearest -> A11 manual two-mip lerp on the global; (B7) the point estimator stratified over the cloud's box, so fine texels were coin flips and a_i was unbounded -> A1's inversion + clamp; (B8) no polar behaviour and no polar fixture -> A4 an ABSOLUTE equal-angle equirect lattice (no cos(lat0) scaling, no anchor) that degrades to the global's mips near the poles, plus a polar fixture and a truncation counter. Warnings adopted: A5 TOROIDAL clipmap windows (each level scrolls by whole cells, the exposed column baked the same frame; the re-anchor full-bake spike and its hysteresis are gone), A6 TIME-based refresh (2 s per level, 60 s global) gated on the MAX of gpu.cloud_profile over a moving fixture, A12 G1 floors per cloud_res arm (693/347/173 km), A13 the level walk + a non-radial instrument for the Chebyshev hand-off square, A14 the column C stored (3 column slices per level: atlas 6144x3584), A15 cloud_res pinned per fixture (the rig config drifted to 2), A16 G4-vs-High reported not gated, A17 an integration stub (constants + a synthetic-pattern bake + stub tap) committed to main BEFORE the implementers start so neither waits on the other, A18 seam scans by image coordinate.
recent_decisions.why: The design's worth is in what the implementers cannot see from their own side: shared layouts, the cost model, and gates that cannot pass on the bad build. The critique reproduced the census numbers itself and found three gates that would have been green on today's speckled picture; launching two implementers on that contract would have produced a merge that looked proven and was not. The amendments are decisions, not a menu, so the revision produces one coherent v2 rather than v1 plus a patch list.

With in-cloud light on clouds seem to almost become completely transparent as the horizon become very easy to see' (the Eddington experiment, default off); (5) 'With warp band off I see a lot more clouds. With it on it seems like most distant clouds vanish' (2.2 km above a deck; the default is ON since v0.1272); (6) 'I notice zero difference with the field walls on or off' (the null instrument confirmed null). Plus a UI request: the F10 panel is now too long to see; make it a scrollable LEFT SIDEBAR, F10 frees the cursor (no alt-hold), a collapse button on its right edge. ORCHESTRATOR READING: (2) is the sun-shadow cache WINDOW (48.6 km fine / 97 km coarse, planet-fixed so it reads as a rotated square): inside it samples read the baked ladder (real in-cloud sun columns, dark bases), outside they read the v0.1288 analytic column (CLOUD_LC_FAR_ANALYTIC = 1.0), which under-shadows a broken cumulus field (a mean-density slant column is far thinner than the in-cloud column: Jensen), so the far field is too bright and the window edge is the seam; the v0.1288 'look identical' check was made only at rain-26km-nadir, a stratiform case where mean and in-cloud agree. Shipped default, top fix. (1) is the deep relaxation starting at trans 0.5 (half the pixel's light still to come) compounding along long horizon slants; the economy's own rule is no look change and it was never measured on a horizon look at half res. (5) is coverage decaying with distance under the band-limited warp (a thresholded band-limited field loses its mean: the same Jensen class the far rung is designed around), so the DEFAULT loses distant clouds. (3) the anchored march is most likely the physically right one (the old march under-counted extinction to first order in h, v0.1271 assessment); the check is for any double counting. (4) the experiment couples alpha to the light source, which it must not; fix or delete. DISPATCHED: workflow wf_de0676a5 (operator-report-v1289): per finding diagnose -> adversarial verify -> implement in a worktree if confirmed and bounded -> review -> repair; the F10 sidebar implemented in parallel (SidePanel::left + ScrollArea, F10 frees the cursor via the existing grab mechanism, collapse tab on the right edge, headless snapshot). Merges are serial (three fixes may touch 40-clouds.wgsl in disjoint regions) and every fix is gated on the rig with the operator's config once their instance exits (one GPU).

Formalizations beyond the amendments: C_11 is identically zero so its channel carries T (the whole column), columns sqrt-encoded with CLOUD_FR_COL_SCALE 12 (8-bit tau steps of 0.008 at the low end instead of 2.0); a date-line crossing is a full refill (unwrapping the index would drift coarse levels); the dev truncation counter is Rust's analytic estimate (0 on Earth: the equal-angle lattice never reaches the 512 cap). recent_decisions.decision: THE THREE FAR-RUNG G0 DEFECTS DIAGNOSED (panel far-rung-g0-defects, 6 agents, 1.5M tokens, 43 min; every diagnosis met a critic that redid its measurements). D1 (window-edge steps) CONFIRMED: cloud_profile_tap's level walk collapses onto one level ('if (La >= Lb) { Lb = La; wl = 0 }') for every sample outside the finest CONTAINED window, which at 873 km is everything outside level 2's 255 km window; rb is then never fetched and the whole edge weight of La goes to the GLOBAL, so each window's outer 20 percent band is a smoothstep to the 19.55 km pooled map and one pixel past the rim the walk lands on the next level pure: a bright strip then a step (the critic verified the geometry on four rims to within 5 px and the band's alpha excess +5 to +20 percent with an sRGB-decoded same-pixel estimator; the contract itself specifies the collapse at lines 288-293, so the code was contract-faithful and the contract was the defect). Fix part (1), approved: re-walk from La + 1 so the band hands to the next containing level; part (2) (dz_pool for the global's samples) REJECTED by the critic: it would change every pure-global sample's element height and move the whole outer disc. Rig gotcha found: every map_diag channel leaves through the sRGB swapchain, so channel RATIOS must decode sRGB first (raw bytes read L + r(6 - L) with r about 0.5; cloud-profile-compare.js measured the wrong quantity). D2 (in-window grain) REFUTED as diagnosed (the atlas's per-texel cloud-count variance, fix = a family-keyed level floor): the critic's decisive control was already on disk, prof-stepinv-1000-r1-eco0 vs -eco1 (same camera, same FORCED level, same atlas cells, only the step economy differs): census 108 vs 2566 in the nadir crop, so the economy's deep relaxation striding across the thin layer's bin in the profile share is the carrier (the per-pixel sample-height phase the diagnosis dismissed); the level-floor fix would also have handed low-altitude horizon samples to the global. Decision: the profile share is exempt from the relaxation and the footprint floor (scaled by 1 - w_pf). D3 (the marched field empties from above) CONFIRMED and UNDERSTATED: the built layer is based at the SLAB BASE (41-cloud-bodies.wgsl flat base at up_m = 0), the march's final sample lands exactly on that base plane where density is identically 0, and the vertical reject in cloud_v2_body leaves the SDF at its 1e9 sentinel so the stride is inert from above: only the ONE comb sample above m1 can ever find a humilis (hit probability h / 928 = 0.11 to 0.22 per ray at EVERY altitude; step_near 522 m already loses 3x at 12 km), and the found ones are skimmed by the economy floors (mask histogram flat from 64 to 208: genuinely partial alpha). The diagnosis's fix was broken four ways (a non-conservative bound that omitted br, a polluted g_v2_top_m read after the sun ladder, ungated effects at every altitude, a gate whose reference arm rendered nothing at 30 m steps under the 224 cap and whose pass bar sat on an arm the fix could not move). Decision: the corrected fix (the vertical gap to the ADMITTED region as the bound; the in-cloud floor at a quarter of the found cloud's height from a snapshotted top) behind a new dev bit (light2_color.w bit 12, F10 'Built-body top bound'), default OFF until its rebuilt gate passes: uniform 60 m reference march (193 steps), full-res map_diag 1 masks at 250 and 60 km, the fix arm within 2 points of the reference, the reference above 20 points. Workflow far-rung-4b (WGSL + Rust implementers, critics, repair) launched on v0.1292.2.
recent_decisions.why: The G0 captures named the defects and the panel named the carriers, twice against the readers' own stories; a fix built on the refuted D2 story would have bought blur for the wrong carrier, and D3's fix would have shipped ungated at every altitude with a gate that could only go green.

recent_decisions.decision: E1 AND E2 DIAGNOSED (panel far-rung-g1g7-defects, 4 agents, 1.0M tokens, 47 min; each reader met a critic that redid its measurements). E1 (over-coverage): the reader ray-traced the dumped atlas through the shader's own walk and law (pixel correlation 0.99 against the masks) and named two levers: (1) the hand-off weight and tap level read the STEP footprint (foot = max(tm * pix_ang, dt * 0.25); the vertical ceiling grows as 1 / cos on oblique rays and the clear-air stride is uncapped), so the profile fires on samples the pixel never handed off, with est's seg_len making a stride several bins of f on one sample; (2) the element law clamps the vertical element to the bin but leaves the horizontal one unscaled, over-counting slant crossings by dz / L_v (4.13 humilis; about 12 on the Low sheet's pooled bins). The critic PROVED lever 1 independently (same-boot 30 km twins: 52 percent of pixels above 8 where G7 demands bit-exact) but showed it is a SUB-BAND LEAK below about 150 km, inert in the 200 to 620 km band where the pixel term wins the max; showed lever 2 is a real law error but nadir-neutral and so cannot explain the forced-level exhibit (a nadir PEDESTAL of +95 luminance at cover 0.9, and a SIGN FLIP at cover 0.55 type 0.46 where forced level 0 is DARKER than the field); found the tracer's own residual (measured minus shipped-law 13 percent crop, 26 percent nadir) unnamed; and found the brief's ladder coverage numbers unreproducible (the r4 masks read 57/69/86 not 80/89/97; the rise is largely the camera zooming into one weather cell). recent_decisions.decision: THE D3 TOP-BOUND NULL DIAGNOSED (high confidence, third attempt after two usage cutoffs; read-only, measured on the v0.1293 gate captures). The easy explanations are REFUTED by reading the value end to end: cloud_v2_body writes the vertical gap into best and publishes it unconditionally to g_v2_sdf_m BEFORE its early return, the march reads it and converts metres by the same factor the body used (no unit mismatch), and the stride margin is about 265 m against gaps of kilometres (it does not eat the leap). THE REAL MECHANISM, in three parts. (1) The published plane is height * sy + br, where br is a HORIZONTAL cluster bounding radius (hundreds of metres to kilometres): a vertical bound subtracting a horizontal radius, so the leap targets a plane one cluster radius ABOVE a 150 to 400 m cloud and never the cloud. (2) The stride then overrides the base comb: the fix arm marches the whole 11.58 km nadir chord in 8.6 samples (1.35 km a step, ABOVE the 928 m vertical ceiling) against the 60 m reference arm s 192; and on exactly the pixels where the bit LOSES a cloud prod had rendered, the fix arm used FEWER samples than its own average (7.6 against 8.6 at 250 km, 13.0 against 15.1 at 60 km), which is the stride carrying the ray past the layer. (3) The value is published into g_v2_sdf_m, which is deliberately never reset when the body path is skipped (harmless for small near-surface distances, fatal for a kilometre-scale from-above gap), so it leaks into samples that evaluated no body. THE OTHER HALF OF THE BIT WORKS: the in-cloud footprint floor cap makes found clouds render MORE opaque, not thinner (the top alpha band at 60 km, prod 0.55 percent, fix 1.96, reference 3.75), refuting the thinning hypothesis; it should be split onto its own switch. AND THE GATE WAS VOID on its own written preconditions: the reference arm reads 8.55 and 8.35 percent coverage against its own 20-point bar, and at 60 km prod sits 1.24 points below ref against a 4-point requirement, so neither a pass nor a fail was admissible from it; the Sahara camera at cover 0.5 humilis does not put enough cloud in the crop to be a reference. FIX (4d, bounded): drop br from the vertical bound, publish into a distinct global reset every sample, clamp a from-above stride to the vertical ceiling so a miss degrades to today s comb, split the floor cap onto its own bit, and re-cut the fixture onto a cloudier camera with a prod-steps twin.
recent_decisions.why: A null result that had survived two cutoffs turned out to hide one wrong term, one leaked global, one missing clamp and a working half, and a gate that could not have adjudicated any of them.

recent_decisions.decision: CORRECTION plus a real authorization hole found by the recon workflow. THE CORRECTION: my earlier claim that "canonical CBOR is not canonical across clients" is WRONG and is withdrawn. Rust DOES sort map keys: to_canonical_bytes (src/relay/core/encoding.rs:18) calls canonicalize, which sorts at :62-66 by length then bytewise, the identical rule to cborMap in web/shared/canonical-cbor.js:96-108. cbor_map alone is unsorted and its own doc comment says so; payload_cbor routes through the canonical encoder. Multi-key payloads are byte-identical across languages, which is exactly why a browser-built proposal verified on the Rust relay. I read cbor_map and stopped one function short. The wrong claim reached a commit message, PRIORITIES, this journal and the operator, and it told a future session to change a signing byte format that is already correct, which would have broken every client at once. recent_decisions.decision: TYPOGRAPHY, v0.1300.0 to v0.1301.1. The operator asked why the project uses so many different fonts and whether one could be cohesive between web and app, then chose the long-term answer on three criteria: user safety, ease of use, global access. Those pick Noto Sans, whose own stated mission is the same shape as the project's. Two evaluations, 33 agents, full record in docs/design/typography.md. THE DECISIVE FINDING WAS NOT ABOUT TYPEFACES: a 2026 Annals of Dyslexia meta-analysis pooled 15 studies, 91 effect sizes, N=688 on special dyslexia typefaces and found g = -0.04, and Marinus et al. 2016 showed why the folklore survives (Dyslexie beat Arial by 7 percent, then they matched Arial's SPACING to Dyslexie's and the advantage vanished). The benefit is spacing, which is a CSS property and an egui parameter, not a font file. SHIPPED: the 24-word seed phrase was a bare proportional label at 11.9px inside a frame whose own comment calls it the single most dangerous string in the app, while main_menu.rs rendered the same words in monospace 40 lines away; eight character-by-character sites now use Hack, including both base64 invite ticket fields, the only strings in the product where 0, O, I and l coexist. Every arrow in the proportional UI was tofu on Linux and macOS because Ubuntu-Light carries 0 of 112 arrows and epaint puts Hack in Monospace only, while U+2192 appears 111 times in src/gui; Hack is now a computed-position fallback in Proportional and four entries left BROKEN_GLYPHS. set_fonts lived inside the emoji success branch so it never ran at all on a machine with no system emoji font. Japanese and Chinese were tofu since no bundled face has a single CJK codepoint; the system-font probe now covers CJK for zero redistributed bytes. The snapshot rig built bare contexts installing no fonts, so 38 pages had never rendered what a user sees and BROKEN_GLYPHS was partly derived from that. Noto Sans is now the interface face on both surfaces, with 8 self-hosted variable woff2 subsets on web. The web dyslexia toggle was both a placebo (a quarter of the studied dose) and a no-op on Linux and Android (fontconfig ships no Comic Sans metric alias); it is now Reading Comfort at WCAG 1.4.12 doses with word spacing coupled to letter spacing. And the star catalogues were verified CC BY-SA 4.0 from both upstream LICENSE files, making stars.csv and stars.bin a second share-alike source shipping in every release.

recent_decisions.decision: SCHEDULED RE-VOTES, steps 1 and 2 (v0.1302.0, v0.1303.0). The Active focus TIER 0 item, built. A cast vote stays immutable and final; revisiting a question opens a NEW proposal carrying supersedes, so the chain is a real audit trail. Schema: three nullable columns on proposals (review_after, review_cadence_ms, supersedes) read off the CBOR payload, with a cadence and no explicit date implying the first review one cadence after close. Reads: standing_decision walks forward from any link, decision_chain returns the ordered history, proposals_due_for_review is what a scheduler asks for and is already idempotent via NOT EXISTS. GET /api/v2/proposals/{id}/chain exposes it, and ProposalIndex now carries the three fields so a client gets the next-review date without a second request. FIRST, THOUGH: the Active focus block named its own blocker, that web voting is a stub needing canonical-CBOR signing in JS. That is false and was blocking its own item. web/pages/governance.html:482 castVote builds a Dilithium3-signed vote_v1, signs with window.pqSignMessage, posts via window.HumOS.pq.postObject and refreshes the tally, and the KAT is src/relay/core/pq_kat_vote_submission.json. Superseding keeps every decision immutable while still answering what stands now, and it makes reaffirmation visible, which is itself information.

recent_decisions.decision: THE CONSTITUTION IS NOW BUILT FROM THE PARCHMENT, NOT THE HOUSE MANUAL (v0.1306.1). The 8-dimension audit of the shipped Constitution returned 32 confirmed findings. v0.1306 had already fixed the missing signature block and the 41 percent footnote contamination, but five independent dimensions agreed at 3/3 on one it had not: Article I Section 8 shipped with NO granting clause. "The Congress shall have Power" lives in a <chapeau> element and the parser emitted only <clause> children, so the entire enumerated-powers grant was eighteen orphan infinitives with no grantee. Chasing that down condemned the SOURCE: the House Rules and Manual also carried three genuine WORD errors that shipped (Amdt XII "and the number" for "and OF the number"; Amdt XII "in presence" for "in THE presence"; Amdt XVIII "all territorIES" for "all territorY"), 14 manufactured "* * * * * *" elision runs inside complete sentences, and 5 invented bracketed subjects ("[Each House may]") printed as constitutional text. Rebuilt from the National Archives transcriptions of the engrossed parchment plus the Bill of Rights and Amendments XI-XXVII.
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked whether the Constitution we ship is "100% as the founding fathers intended". The House Manual is a working procedural text in which the Constitution is subordinate to its annotations; its editorial design (clause splitting marked with three-star inlines, bracketed subjects supplied so each annotated fragment reads standalone) is incompatible with printing a verbatim Constitution. That is not a transform bug and cannot be patched around, so the source changed. NARA holds the original and states its transcription reflects the parchment's spelling and punctuation, which is why the text now reads "Independance", "In witness whereof", "defence" and "chuse". For the operator's literal question, the parchment is the only honest answer.

recent_decisions.evidence: The pattern held all the way down: every pass found errors in the pass above it. (a) The agent writing the tide guide, reading the locale data to write its own document, found hazards.json calling 11.7 ft the "mean tidal range" TWICE. (b) The phenology agent, having to add the months up to build a calendar, found climate.json claiming "December alone (252 mm) exceeds April through September combined (294 mm)". 252 is less than 294. It also found the "roughly 75 percent" wet-half figure is 79.7 percent by that file's own table. Both were mine. (c) The agent writing hemlock waterparsnip found the water hemlock record DISCLAIMING a field character it had a citation for: USDA ARS says verbatim "side veins of the leaves lead to notches, not to tips at the outer margin", on a page already in that record's own source list. Telling a reader a true character is unsourced trains them to discount it. (d) The phenology agent measured something nobody had: a full year of NOAA CO-OPS predictions for Tracyton, validated against Seattle's published MHHW, showing EVERY daylight minus tide at or below -2.0 ft falls mid-April to mid-August, confirmed across four years. recent_decisions.decision: THE LIBRARY REACHED 46 OF 143 TOPICS WITH A DOCUMENT AND 20 COMPLETE EXPERIENCES (v0.1312.10 to v0.1312.16), AND THE SESSION'S REAL LESSON IS THAT EVERY GUIDE NEEDS AN ADVERSARIAL PASS, NOT JUST THE DATA. Eight guides written by parallel writers against a standing brief that now lives on disk at docs/contributor/library-writer-brief.md instead of being re-derived from memory every wave: the sky as an instrument, how an ecosystem holds together, the climate where you live, pests and disease, hand tools, greywater, taking without ruining it, how plants work, metals and alloys. THREE of them were then put to a critic whose only job was to refute, and all three came back with real defects: 8 in the ecosystem guide, 9 in the sky guide, 9 in the climate guide. The dominant shape is NOT a wrong number. It is a correctly-read source restated with its scope removed: the Forest Service said "in coastal Oregon" and the guide said "the Forest Service records", then told a Kitsap gardener that pH 4.3 was their starting number, which our own soil.json contradicts for half the mapped ground here. Second most common is a claim credited to a source that itself credits somebody else (the land-use correlation is Feist et al., and Scholz et al. says so in its own discussion). Third is a check that cannot fail: the sky guide proved "a full moon is due south at its highest" by sampling 23 minutes after the transit and offering the resulting 8.8 degree miss as confirmation. CONCLUSION FOR FUTURE WAVES: a writer's own confident self-report is not evidence. Budget a refutation pass per guide, not per wave.

recent_decisions.decision: THE IN-WORLD SCREENS LADDER STARTED (six rungs, operator-approved). The operator asked for the native app pages (the real inventory page, not the web page) as touchscreens inside the 3D world, a fixed console room in the home populated by those displays, live feeds and movies on displays, real websites on in-game monitors with affiliate links later, and asked whether to embed VLC or build our own player. Answer executed: our own. The ladder, in build order: (1) ScreenSurface, a persistent offscreen egui context rendered into a wgpu texture that a new unlit material type 24 samples in the PBR shader, driven by a look ray (mouse-look) or the cursor ray (free cursor) turned into synthetic egui pointer events; (2) the screen as a machine def (screen: Some((page, px, face, bezel_m, brightness))) with wall_screen and desk_monitor catalog entries; (3) live feed (MJPEG Watch page on a screen, plus an in-game camera through a render_view_onto refactor of the hires screenshot path); (4) the console room: a room-grade zone type, a rooms.ron join that closes the room_N identity gap, a placed zone in the ship structure; (5) a purpose-built video player (WebM/Matroska + AV1 + Opus, pure-Rust decoders, transcode on ingest) instead of libvlc; (6) the readable web (html5ever parse, egui render, no JavaScript, no Chromium, per decision brief 4) as an OPT-IN default-off AppConfig bool, plus data/web/sites.json, the websites/potential-affiliates database whose embed.status field records the legality of embedding each site (needs_review until a human reads the terms and records basis, terms_url, date, name). Testing uses non-affiliate URLs only. Vocabulary: command deck = the mothership bridge; console room (battlestation) = the home workstation; battlestation is also the device role in device-mesh.md, a different layer. Phase 1 launched as a workflow of four worktree builders (rungs 1+2, 4, 5 core, 6 core), each followed by an adversarial critic and a fix pass; phase 2 (live feed, video and web onto the screens) branches from the merged tree. Also found: data/machines/home.ron, data/blueprints/ship_structure.ron and Cargo.lock had sat uncommitted since 2026-09-08; verified as pure serializer churn (the in-app editor re-sorted the catalog, reformatted floats and wrote CRLF; HEAD holds every def; Cargo.lock only lagged the package version line), so merges may restore those files from HEAD without losing anything.
recent_decisions.why: Operator directive 2026-09-16: "Let's do all 6 rungs and can we test without using affiliate links? We just want to get it working in a basic form. We want to make sure people can actually interact with the web display screen in-game. Then we can figure out the legality of embedding the various platforms. We'll probably want a database for it and for the legality to be mentioned in the database for websites/potential affiliates." The earlier answer established that the engine already had every ingredient (ui_snapshots renders pages offscreen with synthetic clicks; the cloud temporal path binds a render target as an albedo; live_viewer already decodes MJPEG; opus is already compiled in), so this is wiring, not research. Purpose-built player over VLC because libvlc is LGPL with its own render path and we need frames in our texture with royalty-free codecs; readable web over Chromium per Brief 4 and the operator's "our own lightweight browser, not CEF" norm.

recent_decisions.decision: WHERE THE FRAME GOES, MEASURED (operator settings mirrored, planet_clouds false, real GPU timestamp queries, 2560x1387, RTX 4070; 21 boots, 72 cost files; captures in the session scratchpad run1..run9). The clouds are not the cost. (1) The planet: gpu.celestial is the frame and it is per-pixel, independent of geometry: 44.5 ms on the moon with six patches drawn, 61 ms at the 400 km limb, 43 ms in the Sahara at noon; shadows, atmosphere scatter, SSAO, god rays and water FFT move it by nothing; surface-detail octaves are 9 to 11 ms and patch count 17 ms only at grazing ocean views. About 12 ns per pixel at 3.55 Mpx. (2) Forest vantages: Fuji grass underfoot 175 ms; near-tree photoscanned models 68 ms (516 trees within 460 m, budget 260), the cluster-card bake about 38, grass strands 17 (83.6k strands, 7.5 M triangles). (3) Low ocean eyes: the water shell pass gpu.celestial_t 42 to 49 ms, independent of sea state and FFT, only the mesh depth cap moves it. (4) The interior: the opaque pass is about 45 ns per pixel: one flat quad filling the view at 0.3 m costs 160 ms; the console room is 76 to 83 ms of gpu.scene plus 14 of transparent (the glass ceiling); the 211-light untiled loop is 8 ms (lights_tiled off in the operator config); the camera wall adds 17 ms only while its wall is in view (its 10 Hz re-render sums into gpu.scene); the six page surfaces and the video decode cost nothing measurable; home-clock-noon is 19.5 ms versus 18.84 on 09-15. (5) Unattributed: at light vantages 13 to 20 ms per frame with no cpu.frame_total or present-wait timer; no timestamp scope on the screen surface pass, the camera sky pass, the particle compute or the sky-view LUT; nothing splits terrain, trees, grass and bodies inside celestial. (6) Oddities: vsync false in config.json panics deterministically at the first settings apply after world entry (ResizeBuffers invalid call, surface configure "window is in use"); [NearTree] recompute logs every frame while parked; the patch-build log prints the constant 24 instead of the live budget. The F10 sidebar root cause (BUG-076): the HUD allocated a full-screen hover rect and egui 0.31 hit-testing stops at the first covering widget rect regardless of sense, so the sidebar below it was unreachable; fixed in hud.rs with a headless test that fails when the allocation returns; Escape now closes the expanded sidebar first, repeated Escape presses are dropped, and debug/ui_request.json drives the main UI for the rig.
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked where the performance goes with the cloud layer off. The 12 fps is the planet fragment path and, at forest vantages, vegetation; the 9 fps in the console room is the interior opaque fragment cost, not the screens. The fixes are a fragment-cost arc (depth prepass and early-z, tiled lights on, a cheaper terrain fragment path, a near-tree LOD ladder), being designed by a perf-expert pass now; the instrumentation gaps and the camera wall at a quarter of its pixels are being built in a worktree.

Cause: set_vsync reconfigured the surface from the settings-apply block at the tail of the frame arm while that frame's swapchain TextureView was still in scope (DXGI ResizeBuffers 0x887A0001, wgpu "window is in use", fatal). Fix on main (3c932421): the mode is recorded and applied at the next frame's start before the surface texture is acquired; two pure tests; the runtime proof (a rig boot with vsync false reaching the world) is queued behind the P1 boot. UPDATE: the vsync-off boot proof ran on 3c932421: the menu-only boot lived 129 s and the world boot 143 s with zero panics, zero surface errors and frames presented (the rig's own config at vsync false, a real reconfigure scheduled every boot because the surface is created AutoVsync); the negative control, the same rig and config with the pre-fix v0.1314.1 archive, died at 15 s in the menu with the exact BUG-077 panic. The applied present mode is now logged at INFO (4c1f75c6).

recent_decisions.decision: OPERATOR, in-game on v0.1317.1 looking at the console room: "can we actually play a video on the red line monitor? This link (a royalty-free YouTube video) ... Or should we play a video that is stored on my PC? Right now it is just a kinda high pitch sound that keeps looping." The sound is the synthetic demo clip (data/media/demo_colour_bar.webm, a tone plus a moving bar), not a fault. YouTube: NO. The screen is our own player (no browser), a YouTube URL is not a file, and pulling the stream would violate YouTube ToS regardless of the video licence (data/web/sites.json embed.status is where that legality lives). Local file: YES, but the player decodes only WebM AV1 + Opus by the codec policy in docs/design/media-player.md (H.264/AAC excluded for patents; VP9/Vorbis not decoded), and there is no in-app way to choose a file. Dispatched one builder for the two rungs the design already names: an on-screen Open control using the existing file_picker_modal (choice remembered per screen in AppConfig; home.ron stays the default), and transcode-on-ingest with the machine ffmpeg (found at C:Apps fmpeg in fmpeg.exe; PATH and common spots searched; ffmpeg_path row in Settings > Media) to a cached WebM AV1 + Opus, with progress on the screen and an honest failure message; a video_open IPC verb, an MP4 fixture, and a rig proof (two snapshots that differ, a cache hit on the second open).
recent_decisions.why: GUI-first: an in-app button that runs ffmpeg under the hood is allowed, a terminal requirement is not. The codec policy is right (do not ship patented decoders), so converting once on the machine is the path the design chose. Platform decoders (Media Foundation and friends) remain a later option if ffmpeg-less machines matter.

recent_decisions.decision: OPERATOR DIRECTION CHANGE: watching YouTube, Twitch, Rumble and similar INSIDE the 3D world on the in-world monitors "is what we want", so the 2026-07-05 "our own lightweight browser, NOT Chromium/CEF" call is superseded for that purpose: build A (our own player on open streams: HLS/DASH plus the OS licensed decoders, Owncast-style self-hosted streaming to united-humanity.us) then B2 (Chromium Embedded Framework rendered OFFSCREEN onto the screen surface through a separate opt-in host process, the platforms official embed players with their ads untouched, per-platform embed.status in data/web/sites.json as the legality record, no DRM). B1 (a docked WebView2 watch panel) is not wanted because it cannot project onto a 3D surface. Route C (stream extraction the yt-dlp/streamlink way) is REFUSED as policy: it breaks the platforms terms, strips the ads that make embedding permitted, invites a takedown against the GitHub repo that hosts our releases, and contradicts the Accord; affiliate permission is a separate matter and is never a reason to extract. The lightweight reader stays for text pages; the engine is used only where a page needs JavaScript. B2 spike dispatched now (host process, verified runtime download, watch page, wall_screen_6 proof matrix per platform); A queued behind the in-flight picker/transcode builder because both touch src/media.
recent_decisions.why: The platforms allow embedding through their official players precisely because their ads play; a browser engine is the only thing that runs those players, and offscreen rendering is the only way to put them on a 3D monitor. Keeping the default build free of the Chromium SDK (a separate host process, runtime downloaded on opt-in and hash-verified) protects CI, the download size and every user who never wants it.

recent_decisions.decision: THE VIDEO SCREEN CHOOSES ITS OWN FILE (v0.1318.0). The Fable usage ran out mid-flight and killed both builders: the video one died partway through rewriting the provider (supporting work done, the file left not compiling), the browser spike died in its reading stage with nothing written. Finished the video rung on Opus: three compile errors (the egui 0.31 Margin is i8; the Ingest::Transcoding variant now CARRIES the reason a file needs converting so the screen can say it; a returned trait object cannot shrink a static box), one test borrow, and three TEST defects that were hiding real behaviour, not code defects: the headless draw helper ran the content ONCE where a fresh surface runs it TWICE (an egui Area settles on the second run, so no control strip was ever drawn and both strip tests failed), the unwatched-film case needed a picture on screen (headlessly no frame decodes, and a screen with nothing to show keeps its strip up by design), and it needed the one last draw that TAKES THE STRIP DOWN before the quiet tick. Live proof in the console room on wall_screen_5: an H.264 + AAC MP4 fixture handed through the dev IPC converted with ffmpeg, played with audio, moved 76,832 of 921,600 pixels between two snapshots a second apart, and opened again from the cache with no second ffmpeg run; verify-screens 12/12, zero panics, 1982 library tests. One near-miss worth keeping: the first verify-screens run failed 11 of 12 with zero panics, which looked like a regression and was the missing dxcompiler.dll beside the worktree exe (FXC boot overran the autopilot window), the same trap the P3 builder hit; stage the DLLs into any worktree target/release before judging a rig failure.
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked a plain question about the monitor in their home and the answer needed both halves: the codec policy is right, so the way to play their files is to convert once on the machine rather than ship a patented decoder. The test defects are the more valuable lesson: all three asserted behaviour the provider genuinely has, and a less careful finish would have deleted or weakened them to get green.

recent_decisions.decision: OPERATOR: "Can I play a DVD that is in my PC on an in-game display?" Their drive is an HL-DT-ST DVD-RAM at F: with no disc loaded. Answer split on ONE line and a builder dispatched for the lawful half. YES for a disc we can read as files (a disc the operator burned, a camcorder disc, a data disc, an unprotected video DVD): the VOB files are MPEG-2 program streams, and the MPEG-2 video and AC-3 audio patents expired around 2017 and 2018, so the codec policy in media-player.md has nothing against them; ffmpeg reads them and the v0.1318.0 ingest path converts them. NO for a copy-protected commercial disc: those are CSS encrypted, and this project will not ship, bundle, call, document or hint at circumvention. That line is firmer than the streaming one: breaking disc encryption is the central case anti-circumvention law was written for, and the message on screen must state what the app does rather than point at a workaround. The increment adds vob/m2v/vro to the picker extensions (never iso, an image is a filesystem), the optical drive as a picker root when a disc is loaded, MAIN TITLE selection over a VIDEO_TS tree as pure functions (largest title set, menu VOB excluded, parts in order, concatenated as one film), an honest on-screen message for a protected disc, a synthesised unencrypted VIDEO_TS fixture so none of this needs a physical disc, and a rig proof on wall_screen_5.
recent_decisions.why: The operator asks these questions in the middle of using the thing, and the right answer is the one that ships the part we can lawfully do rather than a flat no. The distinction also matters for the mission: a family archive on a burned disc is exactly the kind of content this platform should carry, and it is fully legal.

recent_decisions.decision: WRITING NORMS CHANGED AND THE LEGAL POSITION WRITTEN DOWN. (1) The flat em dash ban is now a BUDGET: rare in ordinary prose, and quoted text reproduced EXACTLY, punctuation included. The operator asked for this because the hard ban corrupted a quotation of the US Constitution, which is full of them; changing punctuation inside a quote falsifies it. The lint keeps its teeth for app copy and keeps its emdash-exempt hatch. (2) NEW NORM in CLAUDE.md: when we decline to build something because of a law, a patent or a platform holder rule, say so where the person hits it and say WHICH of the three, because only the first is fixed. Operator: "That way people see it and go oh, okay instead of asking me to add a feature we legally cant." (3) docs/reference/media-stance.md is the public record (what we do, what we will not do, a PLATFORM TABLE so nobody meets an unnamed wall, and a commitment to switch the feature off publicly if anyone objects), and docs/user/rights/laws_that_limit_this_software.md is the LIBRARY page written so the operator can hand it to a lawyer or a representative: the rule, the harm, the mechanism that already exists (the US Copyright Office triennial exemption process, free to petition, how tractor repair and game preservation won ground), and the one-sentence reform (circumvention unlawful when it is a step toward infringing, lawful when the underlying use is lawful). (4) CORRECTED the console framing: the barrier is not fees. Apple is a modest yearly fee and Google a small one-off; console programmes are free to approved developers. The real blockers are approval as a registered developer, non-disclosure terms on the kits that clash with publishing the code, and our size. The operator wants consoles eventually and that intent is now on the page. (5) The disc rung merged: a folder is a disc, main title chosen and parts joined, a protected disc detected from packet headers BEFORE converting and answered with one plain sentence.
recent_decisions.why: The operator is building a platform whose whole argument is trust, and an unexplained missing feature reads as either not caring or an upsell. Naming the rule converts a complaint into an understanding, and the Library page converts an understanding into something he can act on. The em dash change is the more interesting lesson: a style rule stated absolutely will eventually collide with accuracy, and accuracy wins.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1319.0: the disc rung plus the live-screen honest messages and a test publisher. THE OPERATOR FILM TEST PASSED on his own 100-minute AVI (MPEG-4 + MP3, 735 MB): converted in 6.1 min (about 16x faster than realtime), 196 MB out (a quarter of the source, which matters because he cannot afford storage), plays with audio, duration matches to a tenth of a second, 401,355 of 921,600 pixels moving, cache hit on reopen. The live agent found TWO REAL DEFECTS while proving itself: a stopped publisher left every viewer hanging on its last frame still reporting connected (each viewer holds its own Arc, so the broadcast channel never closed; teardown now sends a zero-length sentinel), and a memoized status page could not be searched by the rig because it only redrew when its words changed (a check that could report visible words absent, the same defect class as the setup-is-the-evidence trap). Gate: verify-runtime 3/3, verify-screens 12/12, verify-live-screen 11/11 (live wall 916,492 of 921,600 px moving in a second against a MEASURED 0.00% floor on a static screen beside it), zero panics. FINDING for the operator: Server Settings video_streaming_enabled gates only the CHAT ANNOUNCEMENT that someone went live; the binary fanout at /ws/live/pub is gated by the live_video feature flag which defaults ON, so frames already flow on a self-hosted relay with that toggle off. Also corrected an overstatement to the operator: a screenshot of his own film in chat is not a legal risk; the real concern is a recognisable studio frame in PUBLIC promotional material, and the fix is to demo with the Blender open movies (CC-BY, made for exactly this).
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked two plain questions in the middle of using the thing (can I watch my own film, can I watch a livestream) and both answers needed real work rather than an explanation. The live increment is the more valuable one: it turned an untestable feature into one with its own repeatable check and a publisher, which is also the first real piece of route A (stream to our own server, watch it in world, nobody in the middle).

recent_decisions.decision: THE NIGHT THE GATES CAME BACK ON, plus the browser verdict. Operator asked what to work on; chose the file_size_ratchet extractions over the declared top of TIER 0, because a red ratchet ABORTS just lints at the first failure, so just verify could not run at all and focus_optin_lint, account_sql_lint and rig_pin_lint were being silently skipped. Two biggest cleared by parallel agents, both pure motion proven by accounting rather than asserted: src/lib.rs 19,892 to 16,211 (four modules: frame_ws_poll, frame_shells, frame_water, frame_near_trees; the moved bodies diffed line by line, 1,667 identical lines in the pump, and the 14 and 9 differing CHARACTERS in the other two are dereferences forced by taking a context struct, each listed in its module header) and src/renderer/mod.rs 5,652 to 2,742 (celestial, scene_draw, overlay_draw, surface; all seven create_bind_group sites stayed put, which is the v0.1029 hazard). EIGHT FILES STILL RED (chat.rs +1053, gui/mod.rs +865, api.rs +280, msg_handlers.rs +136, materials.rs +103, capture.rs +67, grass.rs +60, planet_chunks.rs +58) so the gate is still off until they land; two agents dispatched for them. SECOND HOLE FOUND: cargo test --features relay --no-default-features --lib has not COMPILED for some time (about 20 errors, test code calling native helpers ungated), and just verify only runs the native target, so the relay build, which is what CI deploys and the live server runs, has no test battery at all. The msg_handlers case needs judgement rather than a reflex gate: those are the relay DM tests, and gating them behind native means the relay never tests its own DM path. BROWSER SPIKE VERDICT: yes, comfortably. 0.064 ms GPU and under 0.63 ms CPU per 720p screen out of 33; the shared-memory pipe moved 210 MB/s with no read retries in 2,400 frames; the page served from LOCALHOST works, so united-humanity.us leaves the critical path along with the bandwidth and uptime questions. TWO LIMITS: Twitch video cannot decode because the freely distributable engine carries no H.264 or AAC (proven, not assumed: H.264 clip failed, VP9 played), which is the SAME patent line that keeps those decoders out of our own player; and paid streaming needs signatures only its vendor grants. YouTube and Rumble both play. CLAUDE.md amended: the 2026-07-05 no-Chromium rule still holds for READING the web and no longer holds for watching platforms.
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked for a recommendation and the honest one was infrastructure: a broken gate is worse than a missing feature because it disables the mechanism that catches everything else, and the frame loop is also the merge funnel the handbook names as the limit on parallel work, so every line out of it widens the next night. The browser answer needed measuring rather than arguing, and the measurement also killed the architecture question (localhost) and found the one limit nobody would have guessed (Twitch, blocked by the same patents we already refuse to pay).

recent_decisions.decision: THE NIGHT THE SHIPPED BUILD TURNED OUT TO BE EMPTY. Operator went to bed after answering two design questions and asking for cleanup plus boot time. Four agents ran. (1) THE BIGGEST FIND OF THE WHOLE SESSION: .github/workflows/build-desktop.yml copied data/, assets/icons/ and assets/shaders/ and NOT assets/models/ (188 MB) or assets/textures/ (81 MB), at BOTH the bundle copy and the data archive. So every downloaded release has ALWAYS rendered the world as untextured boxes, and only a build run from a checkout ever looked right. This explains the operator complaint "we only have one plant 3D model from the looks of it": in a downloaded build there are zero. Fixed. The size objection does not survive the numbers: we already ship 586 MB of data, most of it sky (241 MB star catalogue, 100 MB galaxy image), all of it read at runtime, so withholding the meshes a player looks at while shipping the backdrop was an oversight, not a trade. (2) BOOT 16.8s to 9.1s median, spread 2.3s to 0.3s, and the fix I asked for DOES NOT EXIST: wgpu 24 advertises PIPELINE_CACHE only on Vulkan, and the DX12 create_pipeline_cache returns a unit struct that stores nothing with no way to read a blob back, so requesting it would have failed device creation (the v0.782 class). The real cost was SERIAL work not repeated work: six cloud PSOs compiling one at a time after the parallel scope closed (invisible because the timing line counted only the other thirteen), a per-planet albedo bake where every output pixel depends only on its own position, and an adapter request that was not slow but CROWDED OUT by twelve noise-bake threads spawned one line too early (2173 ms to 345). (3) PLAYABILITY ASSESSMENT: eleven loops close end to end through the UI today with no console, and 24 of 42 systems tick, so "framework built but not wired" is half wrong; what is missing is the layer between simulation and person (nothing tells the player anything exists, built structures are DISCARDED at exit, fastest crop is 4.7 real hours). It argues the construction tool over hand-authoring on evidence: the four code blockers stopping a second storey are the same four stopping the editor. (4) HOME REDESIGN: the home is 55 x 89 m, 1.21 acres, and 93 percent was ONE OPEN HALL; now 23 rooms. 55 and 89 are consecutive Fibonacci so the shell was already a golden rectangle, which validated the operator instinct for a reason nobody had noticed. The bedroom mirror he described is built. Found TWO DEAD FEATURES: the character-station walk-up matched room ids that never match, and the first fix was also dead (compared action ids against display labels); the capture rig caught both by standing in every room and finding the podium in the greenhouse. NPC reuse was already one line (tile_home_clones), so four neighbouring houses improved in the same commit. (5) CODEC CORRECTION, now a dated findings doc: I told the operator TWICE that Twitch was blocked by patent licensing. The VIDEO half needs no licence (call the OS decoder, which CEF own maintainer documented in 2023 with a dated test, and two forks already do); the AUDIO is the stuck half, and the cost is inverted (H.264 free under 100k units/yr, AAC about $0.98/unit from the first with no cap). US video patents expire Dec 2026 to 2030; EU, Japan, China already clear.
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked for cleanup and boot time and got a shipping defect that had made every download look broken since whenever it started. That is the pattern of the whole session: the size ratchet, the relay test target, the page snapshots, and now the release contents were each silently wrong, and each was found by checking rather than by anything failing loudly. Also two standing rules landed: research a legal question from PRIMARY sources into a dated findings document, and never hand the operator a design doc conclusion as though it were his decision.

recent_decisions.decision: PLAY WAS BROKEN FOR TWO RELEASES AND THE HOME REDESIGN DID IT. Operator: "I tried to log into the game but instead of loading the game world it threw me into the profile page. I can’t seem to get into game." Root cause (BUG-078, fixed v0.1323.0): v0.1322.0 put a standing mirror in the bedroom, source: "profile", because the home is arranged by the rule that a page lives where a person would use it. In-world screens draw REAL pages through gui::dispatch::draw_tool_page against the SAME GuiState the main UI uses, and pages::profile::draw opened by writing active_page = GuiPage::Real (its alias onto the canonical editor). So Play loaded the world, the world drew the mirror, and the mirror navigated the app straight back out onto the Profile page. Fix: a page draw may not steer the app; profile::draw only draws, and the alias is resolved once in the main UI frame in lib.rs. Gate: no_page_drawn_on_a_wall_screen_changes_the_app_page walks the SHIPPED home (data/machines/home.ron), draws every screen that resolves to a page, asserts active_page untouched, and refuses to pass if it checked nothing or if standing_mirror was not among them. Proven red.
recent_decisions.why: Two lessons worth keeping. (1) THE DIAGNOSTIC TRAP: the world stays loaded and ticking behind a page, so the run.log of a FAILED attempt is indistinguishable from a normal session - NPCs moving, position updates, a clean save on exit. Half an hour went into believing the operator had never launched the app, because the log said he had played fine. Do not read ‘the log looks normal’ as ‘the session was normal’. (2) THE CLASS: the moment a rendering surface can show a real page, every page draw is a shared function with two callers, and anything it writes to global state is written on behalf of both. Nothing static could see it - the page rendered correctly, the world loaded correctly, the only symptom was that the game would not start. What found it was driving the real build and reading ONE value back (dev IPC click at Play, then action:state), then doing the same to the previous archived exe to bisect it to a release range in four minutes.
recent_decisions.outcome: v0.1323.0 shipped + v0.1323.1 build-game stamp. Verified on the shipped stable HumanityOS.exe: Play -> active_page None, world_loaded true, Enter lands in first person, 0 panics. just verify green.

recent_decisions.decision: THE HOUSE WAS A DOLL'S HOUSE. Operator, standing in his bedroom: "Seems like either all the furniture is small or I'm just really big", right after "Can we make the TVs larger? The one in the library is tiny and kinda on the floor." He had it exactly right. A machine's size in data/machines/*.ron only ever built the PRIMITIVE fallback box; a machine with a model got that model at whatever scale it was authored at, and this pack is authored at about half real scale (chair 0.46 m, bookcase 0.88 m, desk 0.38 m) beside a 1.7 m eye height. Fixed v0.1324.0 + v0.1324.1: the mesh is scaled UNIFORMLY at parse time so its height matches the declared height (GltfCpuMesh::scale_to_height). Height because that is what a person reads scale from and it survives a model whose long axis disagrees with its declared size (the double bed); uniform because a per-axis stretch would distort every piece; about the origin because these models stand on y=0. Screens also enlarged: wall screen 1.2x0.7 -> 1.8x1.05 m, desk monitor 0.6x0.36 -> 0.9x0.54, with the PIXEL size deliberately unchanged so a bigger panel means bigger text rather than more of it.
recent_decisions.why: Three things worth keeping. (1) THE FIT EXPOSED BAD DATA AS OUTLIERS: every piece wanted a factor of 1.6 to 2.35 except side_table 3.26, shelf 4.50 and pantry_cabinet 4.44, all three declared the size of the thing they are NAMED after rather than the thing their model IS (a coffee table asked to be 0.75 m, a low bookcase 1.8 m, a base cabinet 2 m). tool_rack was a fourth. Corrected; the catalog now sits in one band. A uniform-scale rule is therefore also a data lint. (2) A TEST PROVING A FUNCTION WORKS IS NOT EVIDENCE THE FUNCTION IS CALLED: the unit tests AND the shipped-home gate all passed against a build where the furniture had not changed at all, because they exercise the parser directly. The capture rig caught it. (3) MACHINES HAVE TWO MODEL PATHS: home_meshes.rs rebuilds on a construction-editor change, world_load.rs builds AT WORLD LOAD, and they use different parsers (textured vs not). Fitting only the rebuild path would have left the home small until something edited it and then silently doubled. Anything that changes how a machine mesh is built must touch both.
recent_decisions.outcome: v0.1324.0 (fit + screen sizes + four corrected declared sizes + gates) and v0.1324.1 (the world-load path). Before/after captures in .probe-rig/home-photos/runs/, 0 panics. just verify green. player-home.md known-gap 4 closed; it had predicted this fix and warned it wanted a look, which is what found the second path.

recent_decisions.decision: THE ORBITAL STATIC IS THE CLOUDS, AND I ARGUED WITH THE OPERATOR BECAUSE I READ A CONFIG SNAPSHOT INSTEAD OF RUNNING A CONTROLLED A/B. He reported 'the clouds look weird ... like old TV static'. I read %APPDATA%/HumanityOS/config.json, saw planet_clouds=false, and concluded it could not be the clouds. He had switched them OFF MID-TEST; by the time he posted the five-shot ladder (off / low / medium / high / ultra from one camera at 752 km) it was true again. Meanwhile my own rig A/Bs were invalid: probe-sweep REWRITES .probe-rig/config.json with rig defaults unless --operator-config is passed, so the settings I hand-edited into that file were gone by boot. Reproduced properly afterwards at orbit-tier-873-ultra-r1 with --operator-config: the grainy veil, 17 fps. REFUTED ALONG THE WAY: the land detail octaves (switched to detail_octave_fade_aa on a Nyquist hypothesis; identical captures at 12000 km and 2000 km with and without, so it was reverted) and vegetation (tree/grass density 0 changes nothing).
recent_decisions.why: Three things to carry forward. (1) A LIVE CONFIG FILE IS A SNAPSHOT OF A MOMENT, NOT A FACT ABOUT THE SESSION: the operator is at the keyboard toggling the very setting under investigation, so reading his config and reasoning from it is reading a value that has already changed. Reproduce instead. (2) probe-sweep WITHOUT --operator-config overwrites the rig config with rig defaults, so hand-editing .probe-rig/config.json before a run without that flag is a no-op; the banner says so and I did not read it. (3) MECHANISM, for whoever picks this up: at orbital range the march takes about 928 m radial steps through a deck whose features are ~300 m thick, so each ray is close to a coin flip and the result is per-pixel black and white. Ultra is worst because it asks for FINER clouds at the SAME sampling rate, which can only alias, and costs more doing it (17 fps r1 vs 24 fps r4 at 873 km). Low's straight lines are the painted map's tile boundaries. cloud_res_div (a persisted cloud-dev knob, default 4) is the march resolution divider and the operator is sitting on 2, which doubles the noise and the cost; the r1/r4 twins at 873 km are the standing A/B for it. The real fix is the far-rung increment already merged behind knob 0.
recent_decisions.outcome: No cloud code changed. Findings recorded; the far-rung gates (PRIORITIES v0.1292 block) are the work. ALSO PARKED, NOT LOST: the night-side coast glow has a root cause and a written fix that was reverted rather than shipped unverified. water_shade mixes in water_sky_lut(refl, n_geo) with no daylight term, and that LUT is ONE table rendered per frame for the CAMERA's position, so water on the night side mirrors the day side's sky; coasts specifically because that is where patches are fine enough for `presence` to reach the path. The fix is a smoothstep(-0.18, 0.0, dot(n_geo, sun_l)) factor on the LUT mirror only, wide enough that a dusk sea keeps a bright twilight reflection. Re-apply and verify with an orbital terminator capture; camera_request {body,lat,lon,altitude_km,look_offset_deg} did not aim back at the planet at offsets 0 or 180, so that vantage needs solving first.

recent_decisions.decision: THE ORBITAL CLOUD STATIC: A PROVEN CONFIGURATION THAT FIXES IT, AND A REIMPLEMENTATION THAT DOES NOT. Operator: 'this TV static looking cloud layer is very immersion breaking ... let's apply the fixes.' Reproduced at orbit-tier-873-ultra-r1 with --operator-config. WHAT WORKS, measured: the dev experiment bit 6 (`cloud_wide_edge`) at its DEFAULTS removes the static completely - clouds become smooth coherent masses. Sweep of the multiplier: x3, x6 and x20 are indistinguishable at that cell, so x3 is enough and x20 visibly flattens the deck into a sheet. The near-field guard approach-12km-ultra with the same flags shows no harm. WHAT DOES NOT WORK: promoting either half to a first-class footprint-scaled term. The bit does two things - widens the noise body's carve hinge (40-clouds.wgsl `sw`) and adds a low-density skirt to the constructed bodies (41-cloud-bodies.wgsl `core`). Isolating them (orbit-873-carve-only with rind_wide 1, orbit-873-skirt-only with edge_mul 1) leaves the static in BOTH cases, so they only work together. But reimplementing BOTH, always-on and ramped by the unclamped footprint, also leaves the static in place even at a 20x hinge - and that reimplementation should be arithmetically identical to the experiment at that vantage. So something in the experiment path is not what its code appears to say, and until that is understood nothing ships. Shader edits reverted; the A/B fixtures are kept in tests/visual/vantages.json.
recent_decisions.why: Two things for whoever takes this next. (1) THE FIXTURES ARE THE VALUE: orbit-873-wide-carve, orbit-873-carve-x3/-x6/-x10, orbit-873-carve-only, orbit-873-skirt-only and approach-12km-ultra-carve-x3 are a complete A/B ladder against the standing orbit-tier-873-ultra-r1 cell, all runnable with `node scripts/probe-sweep.js --only <id> --operator-config`. The next attempt starts with evidence instead of from zero. (2) THE OPEN QUESTION IS SHARP, which is worth more than a guess: why does `select(sw0, sw0 * edge_mul, wide_edge)` plus the skirt `select` behave differently from the same two terms applied unconditionally with a footprint ramp that evaluates to ~1 at that vantage? Candidates not yet checked: whether `lodb` at the view samples is what the arithmetic above assumes (log it, do not derive it), whether the sun-ladder and profile call sites pass a different lodb that matters more than the view samples, and whether the dev pad's bit 6 is read anywhere else that was not found by grepping `wide_edge`. MEASURE lodb FIRST - every wrong turn tonight came from deriving a footprint instead of reading one.

The operator has a working configuration today through the cloud dev panel / showcase keys (cloud_wide_edge 1, cloud_edge_mul 3), and cloud_res_div back to its default 4 is a separate independent improvement (873 km ultra: r1 17 fps and heavy grain, r4 24 fps and much less). recent_decisions.decision: THE ORBITAL CLOUD STATIC IS FIXED (v0.1326.0). Cloud edges now widen with the sample footprint: the carve hinge ramps 1x to 3x between a ~170 m and a ~700 m footprint, and the constructed body's skirt is on by default. Both were dev experiment bit 6, which was right about WHAT to do and wrong about scale - it applied full width at every distance, which is why it never became the default. Verified at the operator's own settings across the ladder, panics 0: 873 km ultra clean, 2000 km much improved (speckle remains near the limb and some coasts), 12 km unharmed, forest ground unharmed.
recent_decisions.why: Four things worth keeping. (1) THE MECHANISM: a carve hinge 0.005 noise units wide and a 90 m rind are both far below a 700 m footprint, so a pixel on an edge is a coin flip, and from orbit nearly every pixel is on an edge. Correct mean, binary per pixel, which is what static IS. It also explains why Ultra was worst: it asks for finer clouds at the same sampling rate. (2) THE RAMP MUST READ THE UNCLAMPED FOOTPRINT: cloud_lod clamps at 0 and BOTH ends of the range land there (12 km gives a 25 m footprint, 873 km gives 726 m, both lod 0 after the clamp), so the first attempt gated on the mip and did literally nothing. lodb, not lod. (3) BOTH EDGES MOVE TOGETHER OR NEITHER DOES: isolating each half left the static untouched in both directions. The orbital deck mixes the noise body and the constructed body, and whichever stays hard keeps flipping. (4) THE METHOD THAT FINALLY WORKED, after hours of not working: force the whole thing on with no ramps at all and confirm the look FIRST, then add one ramp at a time and capture between each. Every wrong turn came from deriving a footprint instead of measuring one, and from changing two things per build.

recent_decisions.decision: THE NIGHT-SIDE COAST GLOW: FOUR HYPOTHESES BUILT AND REFUTED, AGAINST A FIXTURE THAT NOW HOLDS IT RED. New vantage `orbit-terminator-3000km` (earth, lat 15, lon 0, time 18, 3000 km) puts the day/night line across the disc and reproduces the operator's symptom unmistakably - every coastline and shallow shelf on the dark side traced in glowing cyan. Run it with `node scripts/probe-sweep.js --only orbit-terminator-3000km --operator-config`. REFUTED, each built and captured and reverted: (1) the water sky MIRROR - `water_shade` mixes in `water_sky_lut` with no daylight term and that table is anchored at the CAMERA, so night-side water mirrors the day side's sky. Gating it on the fragment's own sun elevation changed nothing. (2) The sky AMBIENT, which reads the same camera-anchored table and is also not day-gated, and which would explain the coast selectivity since bright cyan shelf albedo times a small ambient glows where dark land does not. Gating it changed nothing; FORCING IT TO ZERO turned the night-side land black and left the coasts glowing exactly as before. (3) The orbital terrain branch's water emissive (`proc_emissive`, both the glint and the water_shade arms) forced to zero: no change. (4) `water_shade` itself forced to return black, so the near-field water shell cannot contribute: no change.
recent_decisions.why: THE METHOD IS THE POINT, and it is the same one that cracked the cloud static the day before: stop reasoning, force the suspected term to ZERO, and see whether the symptom survives. Two of these four were 'fixed' by gating and looked exactly the same afterwards, which teaches nothing; forcing to zero is what produced information, because it separates 'my gate did not apply' from 'this term is not the source'. The remaining space is now small and worth stating for whoever picks it up: with ambient at zero, the water emissive at zero AND water_shade black, a surface can only be lit by the sun term in the shared tail or by a pass drawn OVER the planet. So the candidates left are the terrain sun term reaching the night side through its terminator window, the atmosphere pass (`30-atmosphere.wgsl`, drawn over the disc and the obvious remaining suspect), or a light that is not the sun. NOTE: hypotheses (1) and (2) are REAL DEFECTS in their own right even though neither is this symptom - a camera-anchored sky table with no daylight term is wrong on the night side whatever else is also wrong - and both fixes are written up in earlier journal entries if anyone wants them.

recent_decisions.decision: THE ORBITAL TV-STATIC IS A LIGHTING DEFECT ON A CORRECT CLOUD FIELD, NOT A COVERAGE ONE. The backlog said 2000 km was "much improved but not clean" and pointed at the far-rung sampling story (one march sample per ray misses a 300 m layer). Captured at the operator's own graphics settings, both halves of that are wrong for the symptom he reported. approach-2000km-ultra is not improved at all: the masses disintegrate into isolated grains. approach-2000km-high, which is the DEFAULT tier and so what every user sees, shows cloud masses with CORRECT, coherent silhouettes whose interiors are filled with per-pixel black-and-white noise. That is exactly his words: "awfully dark and white in spots to the point of looking like old TV static."
recent_decisions.why: map_diag 1 renders the MARCHED coverage alpha as greyscale through the same resolve and composite as content (45-cloud-temporal.wgsl, the screen-path channel bisect). At this exact camera that mask comes back CLEAN: coherent solid masses, crisp edges, zero speckle. So the density field, its thresholding and the accumulation that carries alpha are all fine, and the grain lives in the shading. Checked that the instrument could fail before trusting it, because a diagnostic that renders an analytic coverage instead of the marched one would have proved nothing.

recent_decisions.why: frame_shells.rs derives a coverage floor and a PLACEMENT bypass from the weather condition (Storm = 0.95, 0.95) and fades BOTH by camera altitude (wx_fade: nothing above 120 km, full below 30). The bypass is params2.w, which the shader reads as the fraction of live MODIS placement to abandon for the procedural field, so descending cross-fades the cloud LAYOUT between two unrelated patterns. Root cause is weather.rs holding ONE condition for the whole body with no lat, lon or extent, so the ramp stands in for a spatial term that does not exist. The ramp was itself the fix for the SAME operator reporting in v0.1183 that a local storm painted the whole planet white; it traded a planet-wide artifact for a descent artifact. The covladder-* fixtures pin coverage and type, bypassing the weather path, and stay flat from 20,000 km to 20 km, which is what rules the renderer out. Separately: his HUD going 20C to -8C is temperature_at_player carrying a real altitude lapse, working as designed, and the Clear-to-Storm change was the global sim rolling over during the flight, not altitude.

recent_decisions.decision: ENVIRONMENT REGIONS: the answer to BUG-080 stopped being one more scalar and became a mechanism. The operator asked "can we modularize/layer the params thing so we do not max it out? What else should have latitude, longitude, and size? Not just clouds, but other things too." Both halves have one answer: an uncapped storage buffer of 48-byte EnvRegion records at group 0 binding 4, the same shape v0.782 gave scene lights at binding 1, read by every positioned environmental effect. Three layers on purpose: an analytic base field with locked CPU and GPU twins (temperature, pressure, prevailing wind), a region buffer for discrete transient things (storms, fog banks, fires, outbreaks, aurorae), and per-consumer interpretation so nobody re-derives the geometry.
recent_decisions.why: Packing another scalar into a leftover vector lane buys one feature and makes the next harder. params2.w already means four different things depending on its value (a 0..1 blend, a dev pin at 1, a type pin at 2+tc, a temporal flag at +4), and every camera light pad is claimed through .xyz swizzles a grep for .x never sees. The repo had already solved this once for lights. The RULE the mechanism enforces is the one BUG-080 broke: an environmental effect weight at a point is a function of THAT POINT, never of the camera. The audit answering the operator second question: disasters.rs ALREADY stores position, radius and intensity and nothing outside that file reads it, so a wildfire is invisible; global-but-should-be-regional are weather condition, wind, temperature, humidity and precipitation, fog, pressure, snow and ice cover, disease outbreaks and species ranges, pollution plumes, aurora, light pollution, and ocean currents. He saw something real and named it by the nearest visible landmark, which is what a good report does.
recent_decisions.outcome: NOT FIXED, and deliberately so. atmo_over is always false because the deck must composite after the dome (the cloud march already applies aerial perspective at the first-hit distance, so blending the dome over it applied the same air twice and opaquely; measured 1.2 percent of the disc written with the old order against 99.9 with this one). That rule is right for AIR and wrong for EMISSION ABOVE THE DECK, which the aurora is the first instance of. The fix is to apply the aurora after the composite, which needs the camera uniform and the env_regions buffer reaching a pass that has neither, so it is an increment with real blast radius on a heavily-tuned ordering and not something to land unsupervised. Fenced as PRIORITIES item 1b with two options (preferring a dedicated additive pass over duplicating aurora_emission into cloud_composite.wgsl) and an explicit DO NOT flip atmo_over. Four fixtures carry the numbers as a regression guard.

recent_decisions.decision: THE GRAIN LIVES AT THE TERMINATOR. Profiled orbit-terminator-3000km in ten bands: speckle is 0.55 percent in full daylight, rises monotonically through 11.8 and 27.5, peaks at 40.4 percent at the dusk line, and collapses to about 4 on the night side. It is 73x worse at the terminator than at noon.
recent_decisions.why: The operator said it in one line with no instrument: the clouds are glistening, most noticeable at the dusk line. Mechanically it follows from the bisect: the carrier is the direct-sun term, which is exp(-tau_sun), and at a grazing sun the optical path through the deck is longest and most variable, so the exponential is at its most nonlinear exactly there. The same per-pixel sample displacement that barely moves the result at noon swings it hard at dusk.
recent_decisions.outcome: This INVALIDATES THE VANTAGE every earlier speckle number was taken at. Item 2b and all the 2026-09-22 arms (accumulation off, sun-cone azimuth, sun ladder on the grid, gate recalibration, forced spatial filter, multiple scattering) were measured at approach-2000km-high, which is NOON: band 0, the weakest regime, where a 1.76 percent baseline was being quoted for a defect that reaches 40. None of those results is wrong, and the multiple-scattering finding stands independently because it was a brightness result with a terrain control, but every RANKING of grain fixes done at noon is a ranking in the easiest regime and must be re-run at the terminator before its order is trusted. Recorded as PRIORITIES item 2a, above 2b.

recent_decisions.decision: Measured the price of the v0.1253.2 frozen-jitter decision: frozen jitter costs 4.6x more grain at the dusk line (40.38 percent against 8.68 animated) and buys 6x less fizz (0.34 against 2.09 between two settled captures). Documented as an OPERATOR DECISION in PRIORITIES 2a-i and deliberately NOT flipped.
recent_decisions.why: He ran the original fizz experiment himself and chose frozen, so it is his call; what is new is the price tag, which nobody had measured. The v0.1253.2 choice was made on soft-static-versus-sharp-static at a close camera, not at the terminator where the defect lives. The mechanism is now clear: the accumulator is deep at rest (alpha 0.09 on 88.8 percent of speckled pixels) but averaging only removes noise that CHANGES between frames, and frozen jitters make a parked frame pixel-identical, so a correctly functioning filter was averaging identical values and removing nothing.
recent_decisions.outcome: Also inverted the ranking of the other candidates, which is the wider lesson: the sun ladder on the unjittered grid gave 14 percent at noon and 0.4 percent at the dusk line, while the animated jitter gave 9 percent at noon and 78 percent at the dusk line. The candidate that looked better at noon does nothing where the defect lives. Any grain candidate ranked at noon is ranked in the wrong regime. New tool scripts/terminator-grain.js profiles grain band by band across the terminator, and orbit-terminator-3000km-b is an identical twin captured in the same boot so the pair measures fizz.

recent_decisions.decision: Built the full candidate table at the terminator and found a FLAW IN MY OWN METRIC. Grain at band 5: baseline 40.38, sun-ladder-on-grid 40.22, spatial strength alone 40.22, spatial gate alone 37.54, animated jitter 8.68, spatial forced full 6.07.
recent_decisions.why: Grain is measured as mean absolute deviation from the four-neighbour mean, and forcing the spatial filter to full replaces every pixel WITH that mean. A 3x3 box blur minimises this metric by construction, so part of the 6.07 is the measurement rewarding blur rather than a better picture. The animated-jitter row has no such problem because temporal averaging removes noise without blurring, which makes 8.68 the best HONEST number on the table.
recent_decisions.outcome: Two solid conclusions survive the caveat. Neither the gate nor the strength alone moves anything (37.54 and 40.22 against 40.38), so both bind together and there is no one-constant fix; this CORRECTS the v0.1331.14 note that inferred the strength cap was binding from noon data. And the gate stays shut in the dark because its absolute arm is in raw march-buffer units (sig measured 0.0185 at noon against a 0.25 threshold, and the terminator is darker still), so it closes hardest exactly where the relative grain is worst. Next attempt must FIX THE METRIC first: a grain number a blur can win is not a grain number. All experiments reverted; shader and src clean.

recent_decisions.decision: The still-frame cloud crumb is the density field own structure, NOT march noise. Four arms at one grazing-view camera, scored as mean absolute deviation from the 3x3 mean over bright desaturated pixels: full march resolution 9.22 percent, half 4.89, half with the dither off 5.17, half captured unconverged 4.85.
recent_decisions.why: Every half-res arm sits inside a 4.85 to 5.17 band, which kills three hypotheses at once. Not the dither, because turning it OFF raised the number (at a parked camera the temporal filter has already removed the jitter, and dither-off adds its own mip-ring arcs back). Not convergence, because one second of settle scores the same as fourteen. Not the upsample, because the composite already uses a 9-tap Catmull-Rom under a neighbourhood clamp and full resolution is WORSE rather than better. The practical consequence is that raising cloud_res to cure speckle makes it worse and costs GPU, which is the first thing anyone would have reached for. Recorded as PRIORITIES 2b-0, which gates item 2b: further spatial-filter tuning against a still can only trade real field detail for smoothness, the same trap 2a-ii found when a box blur won the grain metric. The operator complaint is about something CHANGING, so the live question is temporal under MOTION.

recent_decisions.decision: Aurora rework (v0.1331.21): 4 km sheets instead of 100-150 km strands, energy-conserving widening to the full step crossing or one pixel, height ramps box-filtered per step, a 1 - exp(-x) shoulder instead of a hard clip, sRGB-aware triangular dither on the emission output, arcs spread across the oval with half the meander, diffuse 0.22 -> 0.06, sheet gain 20.
recent_decisions.why: Operator: "rubberband on its fat side", "banding ... layers stacking on top of layers", "harsh edges between shades". Three separate banding causes, each proven: 7 point samples of the height ramp (fixed by exact closed-form averaging), a per-channel clip at 1.0 that shifted hue at the boundary (fixed by the shoulder), and 8-bit quantisation of a 3-4 level glow (proven by rendering the diffuse alone at full strength, where the ellipses became a contour map, and by zeroing it). The sheet widening must use the FULL step crossing: at half, samples left gaps and each curtain drew as parallel copies; at the full step smoothstep's symmetry makes them tile exactly and the delivered light equals the true line integral. Cost-neutral (celestial_t 25.80 -> 25.64 ms), because rejection of off-oval and daylit pixels moved ahead of the strand loop. The 8-bit problem is renderer-wide; recorded as PRIORITIES 3b (HDR scene target + one dither is the real fix).

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1332.0: the twinkling specks in space were the space-dust motion cue (lib.rs, data/particles.ron space_dust), not stars. It now spawns only while a movement key is held, and fades out between 200 and 1000 m/s commanded speed.
recent_decisions.why: It ran whenever fly mode was on in space, moving or not, with 1.5-3.5 s lifetimes, so parked it was motes popping in and fading at random: twinkling by definition, wide when close, drifting by parallax. Not rig-verifiable (the rig cannot hold a key); uses the same rate_scale lever rain relies on.

recent_decisions.decision: Cloud sheets increment 2 (v0.1334.0): cloud_synoptic_warp winds the procedural placement and the type coordinate around 5 storm centres per hemisphere plus a jet-shear bump. Rotations only, so area-preserving; mirrored in Rust and property-tested.
recent_decisions.why: Isotropic noise cannot make fronts or cyclones. Measured: blobs became curved frontal bands and arcs; not yet comma heads because the macro octave (~1,300 km) is the size of the storm radius. Kept moderate (twist 2-4 rad) and flagged the tighter-spiral tuning as the operator taste call. Cost +0.3-0.55 ms cloud_screen via HUMANITY_FRAME_COSTS A/B at identical settings. Jet uses a latitude bump, not sin(2 lat), whose shear vanishes at mid-latitudes. Twist tapered to exactly zero at 3.5R because a plain cutoff leaves a few-km step that would print a seam circle at carve scale.

Chose real-time L/min because the plumbing sim and the homestead sizing are real-time; a compressed-time draw (plants per game day) would drain the 8000 L cistern in minutes. Checked the budget first: family home 2.40 L/min production vs 1.35 household, ~1.05 spare vs ~1.0 garden. Tests red on purpose first.

recent_decisions.decision: Crafting depth rung 2 (v0.1349.0): station power. MachinePower::Consumer gained idle_watts (serde default None, skipped when None so editor saves do not churn); machine entities carry MachineType; a StationLoad component holds active/idle watts and the crafting tick sets PowerConsumer.draw_watts to active while a craft runs at the station (auto: its own batch; manual: one powered station of the type), idle otherwise. A manual craft at an electric station with no powered machine of its type is refused with a notice; the Crafting page mirrors it via GuiState.unpowered_station_types. Family home: stove idle 0, oven 2, electronics bench 5, sewing machine 0.
recent_decisions.why: Those four drew ~3.65 kW around the clock, which is not how a stove works and distorted the home power budget. Not done: pausing a running craft when power drops (rung 3). An idle 0 W consumer is disabled by the shedder on an over-budget island, which reads as no power, and that is intended: there is no spare power to switch it on. Tests red on purpose first (no gate; no drop to idle).
